problem: Find the points of intersection of the parabola ${y}^{2}-16x-6y-91=0$ with the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we set $x=0$ and solve the resulting equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-16(0)-6y-91 & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-6y-91 & =0 \\ (y-13)(y+7) & =0 \\ y & =13,-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parabola intersects the $y$-axis at $(0,13)$ and $(0,-7).$
